record.paper_title: Selection Principles and Special Sets of Reals
record.original_question: If X satisfies Ufin(O, Ω) and Y is a continuous image of X in N^N, let G be the set of functions eventually dominated by the pointwise maximum of some finite subset of Y. Must G also satisfy Ufin(O, Ω)?

evidence.quote: Assume that X satisfies Ufin(O, Ω). Does it follow that G = {g ∈ NN : (∃k)(∃f1, . . . , fk ∈ Y ) g ≤* max{f1, . . . , fk}} satisfies Ufin(O, Ω)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}}$ denote the Baire space of functions from $\mathbb{N}$ to $\mathbb{N}$, equipped with the product topology and the preorder $\le^*$ of eventual dominance: $f \le^* g$ iff $f(n) \le g(n)$ for all but finitely many $n$.

For a topological space $X$, an open cover $\mathcal{U}$ of $X$ is called an $\omega$-cover if $X \notin \mathcal{U}$ and every finite subset of $X$ is contained in some member of $\mathcal{U}$. Let $\mathcal{O}$ denote the collection of all open covers of $X$ and $\Omega$ the collection of all $\omega$-covers. The selection principle $\mathsf{U}_{\mathrm{fin}}(\mathcal{O},\Omega)$ asserts that for every sequence $\langle \mathcal{U}_n : n \in \mathbb{N}\rangle$ of open covers of $X$, none of which contains a finite subcover of $X$, there exist finite sets $\mathcal{F}_n \subseteq \mathcal{U}_n$ such that $\{\bigcup \mathcal{F}_n : n \in \mathbb{N}\}$ is an $\omega$-cover of $X$.

Suppose $X$ is a topological space that satisfies $\mathsf{U}_{\mathrm{fin}}(\mathcal{O},\Omega)$, and let $Y \subseteq \mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}}$ be a continuous image of $X$. Define
$$G = \{\, g \in \mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}} : \exists k\in\mathbb{N}\ \exists f_1,\dots,f_k \in Y,\ g \le^* \max\{f_1,\dots,f_k\}\,\}.$$

Must $G$ (with the subspace topology inherited from $\mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}}$) also satisfy $\mathsf{U}_{\mathrm{fin}}(\mathcal{O},\Omega)$?
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not locate a published resolution of this question. The question is posed in surveys of selection principles, and no later paper found in the search explicitly settles whether the closure $G$ under eventual domination by finite maxima of a continuous image of a $\mathsf{U}_{\mathrm{fin}}(\mathcal{O},\Omega)$ space must again satisfy $\mathsf{U}_{\mathrm{fin}}(\mathcal{O},\Omega)$. Status appears to remain unknown based on available evidence.
